title: 第17章 鬼窟宦影第18章 暗涌
content_zh:
暮色四合，大相国寺的钟声沉甸甸地荡开，惊起檐角栖息的乌鸦，黑压压地掠过天际。
君澜与杜若隐身在寺院上空，云层在她们脚下缓缓流动，将下方的一切罩上一层灰蒙蒙的纱。
二人低头看去，但见整座寺院在她们眼中不再是红墙碧瓦、香烟缭绕的庄严佛土，而是一团翻涌着的浓得化不开的黑气。
那黑气从地里渗出来，顺着墙根向上攀爬，像无数条触手在空中张牙舞爪。
“这哪里是寺院？”杜若忍不住皱眉，压低声音，“分明是鬼窟！”
君澜没有说话，目光落在大雄宝殿的方向。
那里的黑气最浓，像墨汁泼洒在琉璃瓦上，将殿顶的脊兽都吞没了。偶有几缕灰白色的怨灵之气从黑气中探出头来，扭曲着，挣扎着发出一声声无声的嘶吼，旋即又被黑气拽了回去。
“这里盘踞的怨灵不下百只。”君澜道。
杜若倒吸了一口凉气。茶灵的灵识也能感知到那些怨灵的存在，它们在寺院里游荡盘旋，有的困在地底，有的附着在佛像上，有的钻进香炉的灰烬里。那些本该被供奉、被膜拜的地方，如今全成了怨灵的巢穴。
“如果这些香客知道他们在这里上香祈福，求的不是菩萨的保佑，而是一群怨灵的垂怜……”杜若看着陆续走进寺院的香客喃喃道。
“怨灵不会垂怜任何人，它们只会吸食生人的精气，一点一点地蚕食，让求佛的人生病、倒霉、家宅不宁，然后再回到这里花更多的钱，求更厉害的符。”君澜淡淡道。
杜若的背脊一阵发凉。这哪里是寺院，分明是一张吃人不吐骨头的网。
这时，寺院侧门的角门开了，两个人影从门里走出来，一前一后。前面的是一个丫鬟，低着头，肩膀一耸一耸的，像是在哭。后面跟着的人是杜五娘。
杜若的眼力好，一下认出了杜五娘。
杜五娘走得很慢，脚步虚浮，像踩在棉花上，每一步都需要春杏回头搀扶。她的脸色在暮色中白得发青，嘴唇没有一丝血色，整个人像一朵被霜打蔫的花。但更让杜若心惊的不是杜五娘的面色，而是她身上笼罩着的那团黑气。那黑气不是在外面附着上去的，而是从她身体里面渗出来的，从她的七窍、毛孔、指甲缝里一丝一缕地往外冒，像烧灼的油脂冒出的黑烟。黑气缠绕在她周身，凝而不散，将她的影子都染成了暗沉的灰黑色。
“她身上有脏东西。”杜若脱口而出。
君澜的眼神微微一凝，她看出了更多。杜五娘的身体里有什么东西在蠕动，不是寄生在脏腑里的虫，而是一种更隐秘、更阴毒的东西，附在魂魄上，像藤蔓缠绕大树，一圈一圈勒得越来越紧。
二人正要跟上去看个究竟，但寺院正门的方向有一团更大的黑气正在靠近。那不是人的影子，而是一团翻涌着的、浓烈的、近乎实质的黑雾，从长街的尽头滚滚而来。所过之处，街边摊贩的灯笼无风自灭，行人纷纷缩脖子、打寒颤，像是忽然被什么东西冻了一下。
黑雾的核心是一辆马车，四匹漆黑的高头大马拉着一辆饰金描银的豪华马车，车帘低垂，看不清里面坐着什么人。驾车的是两个精壮的汉子，面色青灰，眼珠浑浊，像是被抽走了魂魄的傀儡。马车在大相国寺门前停下，车帘掀开一角，一个穿着石青色圆领袍的人走了下来。
君澜的目光落在那人身上：喉结不明显，面白无须，脚步轻而碎，腰间的鱼带和配饰昭示着他的品级不低——宦官。

那宦官约摸四十来岁的年纪，面容清瘦，颧骨高耸，一双眼睛细长而阴鸷，像蛇。他下车之后先整了整衣冠，然后朝大相国寺的山门看了一眼。那一眼的意味很奇怪，不像香客朝拜，倒像主人巡视自家的产业。
了尘不知什么时候已经站在了山门外。他披着紫红的袈裟，手持念珠，慈眉善目，端的是一副得道高僧的模样。看见那宦官，他脚步迎上前去，双手合十，弯腰行礼的姿态恭敬得像臣子见了君王。
“让咱家好等。”宦官的声音尖细，像指甲划过瓷器，听得人牙根发酸。
了尘陪着笑，侧身引路：“大人恕罪，今日香客多了些，耽搁了。这边请，这边请。”
他引着宦官往寺院深处走去，走的不是香客走的正路，而是那条通向禅院的青砖甬道——正是杜五娘来时走的那条路。两人一前一后消失在月亮门后。
君澜在半空中看着这一切，眼中寒芒渐盛。她对杜若道：“走。”
两道身影无声无息地从云端落下，她们跟着那宦官和了尘的气息，穿过一进进院落，越过一道道围墙，最终停在那座禅院的上方。月亮门关着，君澜闭上眼，神识如丝线般向下延伸，穿过瓦片，穿过椽子，穿过天花板，探入禅房之中。禅房里空无一人，但她知道人不会凭空消失，了尘和那宦官一定是去了什么地方，而那个地方就在这禅房底下。
她将神识继续深入，穿过地面，穿过石板，穿过泥土，触到了一层屏障。那屏障不是砖，也不是泥土，而是一种无形的力量，像一张密不透风的网，将地下的一切罩得严严实实。君澜的神识触上去的瞬间，像是撞上了一堵透明的墙，被弹了回来——不是被挡回来，而是被弹回来。那股力量带着明显的敌意和抗拒，像一只被惊动的野兽发出一声低沉的咆哮。
君澜睁开眼睛，面色微变。
content_en:
At dusk, the bells of Daxiangguo Temple swayed heavily, startling the crows perched on the eaves and flying across the sky in darkness.
Jun Lan and Du Ruo were invisible above the temple, and the clouds slowly flowed under their feet, covering everything below with a gray veil.
The two of them looked down and saw that in their eyes, the entire temple was no longer a majestic Buddha land with red walls and green tiles and smoke-filled buildings, but a surging black air that was too thick to be dissolved.
The black air seeped out from the ground and climbed up the wall, like countless tentacles spreading their teeth and claws in the air.
"Where is this temple?" Du Ruo couldn't help but frown and lowered his voice, "It's clearly a ghost cave!"
Jun Lan didn't speak, his eyes fell in the direction of the Great Hall.
The black air there was the thickest, like ink splashed on the glazed tiles, swallowing up all the ridged beasts on the top of the hall. Occasionally, a few wisps of gray-white resentful spirit poked their heads out from the black air, twisted and struggled to let out a silent roar, and were immediately pulled back by the black air.
"There are no less than a hundred resentful spirits entrenched here." Jun Lan said.
Du Ruo took a breath of cold air. The tea spirit's spiritual consciousness can also sense the existence of those resentful spirits. They are wandering and circling in the temple. Some are trapped underground, some are attached to Buddha statues, and some get into the ashes of the incense burner. Those places that should have been enshrined and worshiped have now become nests of resentful spirits.
"If these pilgrims know that they are praying for blessings here, they are not asking for the blessing of the Bodhisattva, but the mercy of a group of resentful spirits..." Du Ruo murmured as he watched the pilgrims entering the temple one after another.
"The resentful spirits will not take pity on anyone. They will only suck the essence of strangers and eat away bit by bit, making those who pray for Buddha sick, unlucky, and restless at home. Then they will come back here to spend more money and ask for more powerful talismans." Jun Lan said lightly.
A chill ran down Du Ruo's spine. This is not a temple, it is clearly a web that eats people without spitting out their bones.
At this time, the corner door of the side door of the temple opened, and two figures walked out of the door, one behind the other. In front of her was a maid, her head lowered and her shoulders shrugged, as if she was crying. The person following behind was Du Wuniang.
Du Ruo had good eyesight and recognized Du Wuniang immediately.
Du Wuniang walked very slowly, her steps were frivolous, as if she were stepping on cotton, and Chun Xing needed support at every step. Her face was so white that it turned blue in the dusk, her lips were without a trace of blood, and her whole figure was like a flower that had been wilted by frost. But what frightened Du Ruo more was not Du Wuniang's complexion, but the black aura surrounding her body. The black air was not attached to the outside, but seeped out from inside her body. It came out from her orifices, pores, and nails, like black smoke from burning grease. The black energy wrapped around her body, condensing and not dissipating, dyeing her shadow a dark gray-black.
"There is something dirty on her body." Du Ruo blurted out.
Jun Lan's eyes narrowed slightly, and she saw more. There was something squirming in Du Wuniang's body. It was not a parasitic worm in her organs, but something more secret and sinister, attached to her soul, like a vine wrapping around a tree, tightening around her.
The two of them were about to follow to see what was going on, but there was a larger group of black energy approaching from the direction of the main entrance of the temple. It was not a human shadow, but a surging, thick, almost substantial black mist, rolling in from the end of the long street. Wherever he passed, the lanterns of street vendors extinguished themselves without any wind, and pedestrians shrank their necks and shuddered, as if they were suddenly frozen by something.
The core of the black mist was a carriage. Four tall black horses pulled a luxurious carriage decorated with gold and silver. The curtains of the carriage were drooped, making it difficult to see who was sitting inside. Driving the car were two strong men with grayish complexions and cloudy eyes, like puppets whose souls had been sucked away. The carriage stopped in front of the Daxiangguo Temple, the curtain opened a corner, and a man wearing an azure round-neck robe stepped out.
Jun Lan's gazeIt fell on that man: his Adam's apple was not obvious, his face was white and beardless, his steps were light and broken, and the fish belt and accessories around his waist showed that he was a high-ranking eunuch.
The eunuch was about forty years old, with a thin face, high cheekbones, and a pair of slender and sinister eyes, like a snake. After getting out of the car, he straightened his clothes and then glanced at the mountain gate of Daxiangguo Temple. The meaning of that glance was very strange, not like a pilgrim making a pilgrimage, but like a master inspecting his property.
Liao Chen was already standing outside the mountain gate at some point. He was wearing a purple-red cassock, holding a rosary in his hand, and had a kind-hearted look on his face, looking like an accomplished monk. When he saw the eunuch, he stepped forward to greet him, clasped his hands together, and bowed in a respectful manner, like a minister meeting the king.
"Make it easier for our family to wait." The eunuch's voice was high-pitched, like fingernails scratching on porcelain, making one's teeth ache.
Liao Chen smiled along with him and led the way: "My lord, please forgive me. There are too many pilgrims today, so I've been delayed. Please come this way, please come this way."
He led the eunuch towards the depths of the temple, not on the proper path taken by pilgrims, but on the green brick corridor leading to the Zen courtyard - the same path Du Wuniang took when he came. The two disappeared behind the Moon Gate one after another.
Jun Lan watched all this in mid-air, with a cold light growing in his eyes. She said to Du Ruo: "Let's go."
The two figures fell silently from the clouds. Following the eunuch and Ling Chen's breath, they passed through the courtyard, crossed the walls, and finally stopped at the top of the Zen courtyard. The moon door was closed, Jun Lan closed his eyes, and his consciousness extended downward like a thread, passing through the tiles, through the rafters, through the ceiling, and into the Zen room. There was no one in the Zen room, but she knew that people would not disappear out of thin air. Liao Chen and the eunuch must have gone somewhere, and that place was under the Zen room.
She continued to deepen her consciousness, through the ground, through the stone slabs, through the soil, and touched a barrier. The barrier is not bricks or soil, but an invisible force, like an airtight net, covering everything underground tightly. The moment Jun Lan's consciousness touched it, it was as if he had hit a transparent wall and was bounced back - not blocked, but bounced back. That force carried obvious hostility and resistance, like a startled beast that let out a low roar.
Jun Lan opened her eyes and her expression changed slightly.
